title: Sausage & Tomato Rigatoni
subtitle: mild Italian sausage in a quick tomato-cream sauce, tossed with rigatoni and Parmesan
imageAlt: Rigatoni with crumbled sausage in a pink tomato sauce and Parmesan in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Buy mild (not hot) Italian sausage. Slit the casings and squeeze the meat out.

steps.title: Water on
steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the salt.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the sausage meat, breaking it up, 7–8 minutes until browned and no pink remains (71°C / 160°F). Spoon off all but 1 tbsp fat.

steps.title: Onion and garlic
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and cook 5 minutes, then the garlic and Italian seasoning for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, sugar and salt and simmer 10 minutes. Meanwhile, cook the rigatoni until al dente; save 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir the cream into the sauce, then add the rigatoni and the Parmesan and toss over low heat, adding pasta water a splash at a time until glossy.

fixIt.fix: Spoon off the sausage fat before the onion goes in.
Loosen with pasta water; it thickens fast as it sits.
Sausage is salty; taste before adding the ½ tsp salt.

saleTip: Mild Italian sausage is often $5 a pack at No Frills; rigatoni and penne go on sale 2 for $3.
leftovers: Reheat with a splash of milk or water to loosen.
doneness: Sausage meat cooked to 71°C (160°F) with no pink (Health Canada, ground pork). Reheat to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested sausage-and-tomato-cream pasta methods (Canadian Living, Bon Appétit): browned sausage, crushed tomato sauce finished with cream, Parmesan and pasta water.
prepAhead: The sauce keeps 3 days in the fridge; cook the pasta fresh.
reheat: Covered in a pan over medium-low with a splash of milk or water, stirring, or in the microwave 2 minutes, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Sausage and tomato sauce with Parmesan; no cream.

stepNotes.4: Basic: no cream; toss with the Parmesan and pasta water.

fancy.note: Creamy ricotta dollops and extra Parmesan on top.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Top each bowl with a spoon of ricotta and a sprinkle of the extra Parmesan.

plating: A spoon of cold ricotta on the hot pasta.
Black pepper and Parmesan over the top.

why.1-1: Sausage is already seasoned, so the sauce tastes slow-cooked in 25 minutes.
why.0-0: Rigatoni's wide ridged tubes catch the sauce and bits of sausage.
why.1-6: A little sugar softens the acidity of canned tomatoes.

funFact: Rigatoni comes from the Italian 'rigato', meaning ridged or lined.

keeps.note: cream sauces turn grainy when frozen

drink: A Chianti or Montepulciano, or a San Pellegrino aranciata.
